children: Kosovo’s economy grew 4.06% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, slowing from a downwardly revised 5.27% expansion in the previous quarter.
Growth was broad-based across sectors, with wholesale and retail trade, repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles, transport and storage, and accommodation and food service activities rising 3.48%.
Financial and insurance activities also increased sharply, by 15.67%.

Additional growth came from information and communication (5.04%), arts, entertainment and recreation, household production activities for own use and other service activities (1.29%), scientific, professional and technical activities and administrative and support service activities (3.99%), and manufacturing (3.48%).
From the expenditure side, exports of goods and services had the largest impact, rising 6.82%, while gross fixed capital formation increased 11.91%.
Government spending rose 7.02%, while household consumption increased 4.4%.

title: Kosovo GDP Growth Slows to 4.06% in Q2
